scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, England sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 68 from Joe Root, complemented by a commanding 126-run stand between DM Bess and Jos Buttler that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.93 RPO. Pakistan's bowling response was spearheaded by Mohammad Amir (4/36), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. England's total of 242/10 (82.1 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

Pakistan embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 64 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. Haris Sohail anchored the innings with a resolute 39, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. James Anderson (1/12) maintained tight lines for England, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 66/1 (12.4 ov), Pakistan successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Lord's commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 184/10 (58.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 363/10 (114.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 126-Run Stand: DM Bess & Jos Buttler, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Mohammad Abbas delivered a masterclass for Pakistan (5 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Pakistan 52%) and allowing Pakistan to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Pakistan's bowling unit, bolstered by Mohammad Amir (24 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Pakistan won by 9 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Pakistan's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, Pakistan won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
